objective.value: Extend the FLEX-1 results to fuels and atmospheres that mimic real combustor conditions and provide benchmark data on bi-component droplet combustion over a wide range of initial conditions, in order to validate numerical simulations and develop new theoretical models. Specific aims: liquid-phase mixing in bi-component droplets; steady and unsteady liquid- and gas-phase phenomena; flame extinction mechanisms and their boundaries; soot formation and soot-shell dynamics; and the influence of droplet interactions on the flammability limits and extinction of droplet arrays.

relevance_notes.value: FLEX-2 studies flame extinction mechanisms and the flammability limits of liquid-fuel droplet arrays in microgravity, and provides benchmark data for validating droplet-combustion models. That is relevant to spacecraft fire suppression and to understanding material/fuel flammability in the oxygen-enriched, reduced-pressure atmospheres planned for a lunar base and pressurized rovers.
